_comment: The GPU types the pool knows. names: every string nvidia-smi prints for the type. vram_mib: the nominal size; a card is accepted inside nominal x [0.90, 1.05] unless vram_mib_min / vram_mib_max give a measured window. counts: the box sizes admitted for the type (a rental takes the whole box); default [1, 2, 4, 8]. status: qualified = admitted; listed = known but not admitted. Only the RTX5090 has been run on a real card. The other six are admitted on Lium's names and sizes (gpu_spec_table.py, 10/5) and on the proof built for their architectures, not yet on a run of our own: confirm each on a real card before the compute share pays. RTXPRO6000 carries a floor of 95000 MiB (both editions report 97887): at the default 0.90 floor the proof's fill floor for it would sit inside an H100's window.
